newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Angry Belgrade pensioners demand their money.
newsitem.headline: Angry Belgrade pensioners demand their money.

text.p: Thousands of angry pensioners braved blistering heat to block Belgrade city centre on Thursday in protest at delays in paying their state allowances.
"We have sunk to the lowest possible level. We are fighting for subsistence," Milan Djuric, president of the Serbian Independent Pensioners' Association told the rally.
"They owe us two and half months' pension while forcing us to pay all our bills regularly," he added.
Djuric said more than 250,000 pensioners could not pay their monthly bills while at least 600,000 could not even afford basic needs.

The country's 1.6 million pensioners, who cost the ruling Socialists some 400 marks ($218) each a month, are a huge burden for empty state coffers and an idle economy which now operates at only 40 percent of capacity.
According to a recent survey, three million of the country's 11 million population are poor and another 600,000 are starving.

The government has said it would earmark 100 million marks for late pension payments from the Development Fund, the only recipient of some 1.5 million marks raised through a partial sale of phone company Telekom Srbija to foreign companies.
It wants to avoid a threatened wave of strikes and protests by pensioners, teachers and doctors ahead of elections on September 21.
But pensioners vowed they would not support those who pushed them into misery.
"After 30 years of work I can only afford one loaf and a litre of milk a day," said Branko Monasevic, a retired university professor.
"I hope I will live to see the day when (Yugoslav President Slobodan) Milosevic and his mafia leave."
Economic analysts have called for a shake-up of public spending and especially pensions as a priority for the next government.
They estimate pensions this year will account for some 20 percent of the country's targeted gross domestic product (GDP) of 103.28 billion dinars ($21.3 billion).
